program.name: ENS Service Provider Program, Season 3 (SPP3)
program.authority: ENS DAO, following a named SPP3 committee recommendation ratified by on-chain executable vote

rules.description: The public cohort record states that one application failed the eligibility gate and the remaining 25 were scored; Goldsky appears among the scored and selected providers. This record represents only the aggregate fact that Goldsky passed the published pre-score hard screen.

eligibility.rationale: Eligibility is derived from the public process statement that only applications passing the hard screen were scored and from Goldsky appearing in the published scored cohort.

evidence.description: SPP3 program authorization and committee model.
Published SPP3 submission timeline, hard eligibility screen, and weighted evaluation rubric.
Published SPP3 cohort recommendation naming Goldsky for a $450,000 indexing award (Option B scope), aggregate scores, and delivery/milestone framing.
Public proposal mirror reporting the executed four-provider SPP3 cohort including Goldsky.
Goldsky application URI linked by the public cohort recommendation. Content beyond the cohort summary is not asserted from retrieval.

materialFindings.statement: The published committee assessment reports Goldsky C1 Prior Delivery mean score as 4.0.
The published committee assessment reports Goldsky C2 Scope Clarity mean score as 3.8.
The published committee assessment reports Goldsky C3 Milestone Structure mean score as 3.4.
The published committee assessment reports Goldsky C4 Adoption, Revenue, and Ecosystem Utility mean score as 3.3.
The published committee assessment reports Goldsky weighted subtotal as 3.37, with the 5% discretionary component excluded.

The committee recommended a $450,000 Goldsky award for ENS indexing as a dedicated public service under the expanded Option B scope the team confirmed before selection, treating indexing as a standalone mandate.

evaluation.aggregateScale: published weighted subtotal out of 4.75; 5% discretionary component excluded

decision.rationale: The executed cohort proposal ratified the four selected SPP3 providers. Goldsky was allocated $450,000 following the committee recommendation and published assessment.
decision.quorum: 130.99% displayed by the public proposal mirror

challenge.scope: The reviewed public governing and cohort artifacts did not identify a dedicated post-decision factual or procedural correction path for this provider-selection decision. This is a public-evidence statement, not a claim that no private or internal process existed.

deliveryConditions.description: Operate ENS indexing as a dedicated public service under the negotiated SPP3 Award Notice for the Option B scope confirmed before selection; maintain required reporting during the funded cycle.
deliveryConditions.reviewWindow: Quarterly reporting across the 12-month SPP3 cycle
deliveryConditions.verificationMethod: Published or institutionally reviewed quarterly reporting and committee/Foundation oversight under the SPP3 terms and Award Notice.
deliveryConditions.verifier: SPP3 committee and ENS Foundation, according to the public program terms and provider Award Notice
dependencies: Successful KYC checkpoint and signed Award Notice before stream activation
Explicit commitment to the full Option B indexing scope confirmed before selection
deliveryConditions.consequence: The public program terms permit stream suspension or termination for abandonment, reporting failure, or other defined breaches, subject to notice/response terms in the agreement.

notes: Public-only retrospective reconstruction; this is not a contemporaneous institutional decision record.
governingPolicy.effectiveAt and eligibility.checkedAt are intentionally null because exact timestamps were not established from the reviewed public sources.
Goldsky-specific provider milestones beyond the public Option B / indexing mandate summary and C3 score are not reconstructed from inaccessible Award Notice or application bytes.
No Goldsky-specific recusal is disclosed in the reviewed public cohort text; the Namespace-only recusal is not attributed to this case.
Reference-only remote sources are not represented as exact byte-preserved captures.
